title: Wed 4 Nov: Nifty's fourth straight gain as foreign buyers return
description:
Hot topic: the Nifty rose 1.6% for a fourth straight gain as foreign investors bought the most shares in a year, but US futures slipped on midterm results. Then: oil, the US vote, the rupee, SBI, Asian Paints, AMD, Airtel, gold and FMCG.

1. Nifty rises 1.6% to 23,811 for a fourth straight gain as FMCG and private banks lead (IIFL Securities / Business Standard; Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
2. Brent settles 1.1% lower at 103.60 dollars despite a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island (Stock Titan / Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
3. US midterm results arrive; Democrats favoured to win the House, Senate close (Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
4. Rupee gains 13 paise to 94.71 as foreign buyers return (PTI via HDFC Sky / Business Standard)
5. SBI's profit rises 14% to 23,038 crore rupees on one-off gains, but the stock falls 1.7% (IIFL Securities)
6. Asian Paints jumps 4% as cheaper crude eases raw-material costs (IIFL Securities / Stock Titan)
7. Indian IT weighs AMD's 45% revenue jump and Apple's margin warning (AMD 8-K, SEC / Stock Titan; Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
8. Bharti Airtel climbs 3.8% two days before its results (IIFL Securities / Business Standard)
9. Gold slips 0.8% to about 3,939 dollars as yields rise (Vista Partners / Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
10. FMCG leads the market as Nestle, Tata Consumer and ITC rally (IIFL Securities / Business Standard)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated with open-source Kokoro voices. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm P.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm S. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: the Nifty's fourth straight gain, powered by the biggest foreign buying in a year.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: S, what happened on Tuesday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty closed at 23,810.85, up 1.58%. The Sensex rose 1.62% to 76,917.85. That's more than 4% in four sessions.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And the fuel: FIIs bought 6,837 crore rupees of shares, the most in a single day since October 2025. DIIs sold 3,679 crore.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved the index?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: FMCG led, up 3.65%, then realty at 2.33% and private banks at 1.98%. HDFC Bank rose 3.6%. BSE was the top Nifty gainer, up 5%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Only PSU banks, down 1.27%, and metals, down 0.14%, fell.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Four days, 4%. Isn't this rally getting tired?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. Foreign money is back in size, partly on bets of a long-term capital-gains tax cut. But the hourly RSI is above 80, which is overbought.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And overnight cues are softer. S&P 500 futures slipped 0.5% and Nasdaq futures 0.9% as US midterm results came in.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what's the trigger to watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: 5paisa flags the 24,000 zone as the next resistance and about 23,480 as support. Foreign buying continuing is the key.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Nestle India and BSE. Sentiment: positive, with caution on the open.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: oil whipsaws on a US strike in Iran.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent traded as high as about 105.7 dollars after reports of US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, but settled 1.12% lower at 103.60 dollars.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Why did it fall, after a strike?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Traders weighed Qatar-mediated talks. Reuters calls oil near a four-week low, with WTI near 95.6 dollars in Asian trade.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: oil near 100 to 106 dollars instead of 115 eases India's import bill, the rupee and inflation. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: BPCL, IOC, ONGC, IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: America's midterm results are coming in. Why should I care?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Democrat Jon Ossoff won re-election in Georgia and Mark Warner held Virginia. Reuters says Democrats are favoured to win the House.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Senate is close, with at least nine competitive races. Democrats need a net gain of four seats.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the bond market?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The US 10-year yield closed about 4.95%, up about 5.8 basis points after a strong JOLTS jobs-openings report.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: control of Congress shapes US spending room, which feeds Treasury yields and money flows into India. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: the rupee finally gets some help.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee settled at a provisional 94.71 per dollar, 13 paise firmer than Monday's 94.84, after touching 94.60.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's driving it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign buying and a softer dollar. Mirae Asset Sharekhan expects a range of 94.40 to 95.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee lowers India's oil import bill, but trims rupee revenue for IT exporters. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: SBI's profit rose 14%, and the stock fell. Explain.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Standalone profit rose 14.3% to 23,038 crore rupees. But exceptional gains were 7,289 crore, and operating profit fell 1.4%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The stock slid from about 1,006 rupees to close at 970.25, down 1.7%. Nifty PSU Bank fell 1.27%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the market now judges state-run banks on core earnings, not stake-sale gains. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: SBI, Bank of Baroda, PNB, Canara Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: Asian Paints jumps 4%, without new results.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It rose 3.99% to 2,437.80 rupees, among the top five Nifty gainers, as cheaper crude eased worries about its petroleum-based inputs.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Wasn't the last quarter weak?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Yes. Profit grew 8% to 1,068 crore rupees and missed estimates. This move is about oil, not earnings.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: crude is a large share of paint makers' raw-material costs, so oil swings the whole sector. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Asian Paints, Berger Paints, Kansai Nerolac.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: AMD's numbers are huge. Good news for Indian IT?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Revenue rose 45% to 13.4 billion dollars, with data-centre sales up 97% to 8.5 billion. It guided about 17 billion dollars next quarter.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Apple fell 1.9% on a weaker margin outlook. Nifty IT gained just 0.34% on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: strong AI chip demand helps hardware, but lately reads as a threat to IT services' traditional work. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Wipro.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: Airtel rallies two days before results.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Bharti Airtel rose 3.77% to 2,065 rupees, adding about 46,900 crore rupees of market value.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: With HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, it made up nearly half the Nifty's 2.4 trillion rupee market-cap gain.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's the number to watch Thursday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: ARPU, against Jio's 218.8 rupees. Airtel reports on 5 November.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Airtel is the Nifty's second-largest stock, so its results day moves the index. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Bharti Airtel, Indus Towers, Vodafone Idea.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: gold slips as yields climb.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: COMEX gold settled at about 3,938.70 dollars, down 30.90 dollars or 0.78%, as Treasury yields rose after the JOLTS report.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It had rebounded from a one-year low on Monday, after a 6.8% fall in October.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: gold prices drive jewellers' inventory gains and India's import bill. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Last one. Story ten: FMCG has its best day in weeks.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty FMCG rose 3.65%. Nestle India gained 4.47%, Tata Consumer 4.29% and ITC 2.82%. Marico jumped about 10% after its results.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Is this the start of a trend?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Not everyone thinks so. Motilal Oswal's Siddhartha Khemka still rates FMCG neutral to underweight, citing cost pressures and weak rural demand.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the rotation into staples shows where money moves as oil eases, ahead of Diwali. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: ITC, Nestle India, Tata Consumer, Marico.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: whether the Nifty holds 23,480 or tests 24,000, the US Senate count, and Brent around 105 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
